query: How does resolution time vary by agent and issue type?

per_column.name: assigned_agent
per_column.rationale: Directly names the agent dimension in the query. Well-separated categorical values with balanced counts across several named agents, enabling clean grouping of resolution_time by agent.

per_column.name: issue_category
per_column.rationale: Realises the 'issue type' dimension. Interpretable, well-separated categories (email, network, VPN, database, etc.) that can be segmented and compared against resolution_time.

per_column.name: resolution_closure_match
per_column.rationale: A near-constant boolean (478 true vs 22 false) that is a derived data-quality flag rather than an external associational variable. The extreme imbalance means no meaningful comparison of resolution_time can be drawn across its categories.

judge.rationale: Two of the three added columns directly and cleanly realise the query's two requested segmentation dimensions (agent and issue type) with interpretable, well-separated, balanced categories ideal for exploratory comparison against resolution_time. The third column is a near-constant quality-flag that adds no exploratory value. As a set, the columns strongly support the intended analysis, discounted only by the one uninformative near-constant column.
